Disney's original private island: a protected lagoon, three separate beaches, and a complimentary BBQ lunch included in every stop. — Quick facts At a glance Opened 1998 Location Bahamas Size ~1,000 acres Dock type Direct pier, no tender Beaches 3 Lunch Included, BBQ style — The island What's there Castaway Cay is Disney Cruise Line's private island in the Bahamas, and the ship docks directly at a pier — no tender boat required, which means faster, easier access than most cruise-line private islands. The island is split into three beach areas: two family beaches (connected by tram and walking paths) and Serenity Bay, reserved for guests 18 and older. The water throughout is shallow and calm, protected by a breakwater, which makes it easy and safe for young kids. A complimentary BBQ lunch is served at both the family beaches and Serenity Bay between roughly 11:30am and 2:00pm — grilled chicken, burgers, hot dogs, fish, and sides, with non-alcoholic drinks included. You never have to return to the ship for lunch, though the option is there if you'd rather. — Free to do Included activities Pelican Plunge — a free floating inflatable water play structure just off the family beach Snorkeling in the designated lagoon (bring your own gear, or rent equipment for a fee) — includes sunken Disney-themed props A 5K running course around the island (free, self-guided) Hammocks, lounge chairs, and umbrellas throughout all three beaches Character meet-and-greets in tropical attire — check the Navigator app for times — Worth booking early Cabanas Castaway Cay has roughly 20–21 family beach cabanas plus about six adult cabanas at Serenity Bay — roughly 325 square feet each, with lounge chairs, a hammock, a stocked cooler, and complimentary snorkel gear. Family beach cabanas run roughly $450–600/day; Serenity Bay cabanas start around $600+/day. They're genuinely worth it for a large group wanting guaranteed shade and privacy, but they sell out within minutes of the booking window opening — typically 75 days before sailing for the general public, earlier for higher Castaway Club tiers. — Cabana countdown Enter your sail date and Castaway Club tier to see when cabana booking typically opens. Sail date Tier Concierge Pearl (25+ sailings) Platinum Gold Silver First-time guest Show cabana window Full Port Adventures + specialty dining windows: Booking window helper . — Which island? Castaway Cay vs Lookout Cay Castaway wins for classic Disney magic, snorkeling, and toddler logistics. Lookout Cay wins for bigger beaches, Bahamian culture, and photos. Full head-to-head: Read the island comparison — Worth knowing Planning tips Bring your stateroom key card and comfortable shoes if you plan to run the 5K Beach towels are provided at the pier — no need to pack your own The family beaches get crowded near the tram stop; walking 5–10 minutes further usually finds quieter spots Food is free at both BBQ locations; bar drinks and specialty items are not — Watch From Founding Cruise Experts Port walkthroughs and tips from independent Disney cruise creators — credited with a link back to their channel when available. pages.description: Grand Cayman Disney Cruise Line port guide: tender timing, Stingray City, Seven Mile Beach, downtown George Town, food, shopping, safety, and what not to miss.

Often a tender port, which changes your whole day math. Stingray City and Seven Mile Beach are the headline draws — plan the boat ride back with real buffer. — Quick facts At a glance Region Cayman Islands Dock type Tender (usually) Currency KYD / USD OK Language English Best known for Stingray City Common on Western Caribbean — The day Pick one job for the day Grand Cayman rewards a single clear plan more than most ports, because tendering adds a variable you can’t fully control. Pick Stingray City / sandbar , Seven Mile Beach , or downtown George Town — and check the Navigator app for tender status before you commit to a tight schedule. Signature day Stingray City / sandbar Shallow-water stingray encounters by boat, often paired with a snorkel stop. The boat ride itself is part of the day — budget real time for it. Classic beach Seven Mile Beach Wide, calm, powder-soft sand a taxi ride from the tender dock. Public access points and beach clubs both work well with kids. Low transfer Downtown George Town Duty-free jewelry and watches, a short walk from where the tender drops you — good for a shorter, lower-effort call. — Disney vs independent What to book, what to skip Book Disney when: you’re doing Stingray City / boat tours — tender timing plus boat schedules stack risk; the ship-wait guarantee matters more here. Go independent when: Seven Mile Beach or George Town with a taxi plan and a tender-buffer reverse plan from last tender, not just all-aboard. Skip: stacking stingrays + a long beach club + downtown shopping. Tender lines punish ambition. Skip: assuming “we’ll just grab the next tender” at peak return — leave earlier than feels necessary. — Transportation How far is everything? Destination From the tender dock How most families go Notes Downtown George Town Short walk Walk Tender lands you right into the shopping district Seven Mile Beach ~10–20 min Taxi or beach-club shuttle Agree the fare and a fixed pickup time before you settle in Stingray City / sandbar Boat trip, ~20–30+ min each way Booked boat tour (Disney or independent) The transfer is the excursion — factor both boat legs into your return math Rum Point / East End 30–60+ min Taxi, tour van, or boat Long transfer for a short call — usually a full-day commitment Tender timing is the real risk. Grand Cayman is a common tender port. Rough seas can slow or suspend tender service, and lines back to the ship build fast near the end of the call — leave more buffer than a pier port. Taxis. Available near the dock for Seven Mile Beach and downtown. Confirm price before loading. Disney transfer. Worth it for Stingray City boat days, since the ship-wait guarantee matters more when your return route includes open water. See Grand Cayman Port Adventure filters . — Food What to eat ashore Beach bars. Casual grill food and cold drinks along Seven Mile Beach — the easy call for a swim day. Downtown George Town. A few sit-down spots near the tender dock for jerk, seafood, or a quick lunch before you head back. Boat tours. Some Stingray / sandbar trips include light snacks or water — check your specific tour, don’t assume a full meal. Kids. Beach-club style menus with familiar options beat a long taxi search when everyone’s already wet and hungry. — Shopping What’s worth bringing home Duty-free jewelry and watches. George Town is known for it — compare prices to home before assuming “duty-free” means “cheapest.” Local rum and coffee. A lower-stakes souvenir than jewelry, and easy to pack. Pressure pitches. Some downtown stores push hard on cruise-day “specials.” You can browse, compare, and walk without buying on the spot. — Safety With kids in daylight Grand Cayman is generally low-crime and tourist-friendly in daylight downtown and beach areas. Stingray encounters are guided and shallow, but listen to crew — don’t chase or grab the animals, and keep small kids within arm’s reach. Boat days mean real water: confirm life jackets fit kids properly and ask about swim-comfort requirements before booking. Sun exposure on the sandbar and open boats is intense — reef-safe sunscreen, hats, and water matter more here than on a shaded downtown walk. — Timing Work backward from all-aboard Day type Realistic clock Buffer tip Downtown only 1–3 hours Easy buffer, but still budget tender wait time on both ends Seven Mile Beach Half day Fix a taxi pickup time; don’t rely on flagging one down at peak return Stingray City / sandbar tour Half day Build in extra margin for both boat legs plus tender lines back to the ship Rum Point / far East End Most of the call Only with a wide call window and a booked, ship-wait-covered tour — Don’t miss this Tender ports punish last-minute plans. Confirm tender status and last-tender time in the Navigator app the morning of, and treat the posted all-aboard as your real deadline — not the last tender time, since lines build. — Don’t miss The one thing repeats push Do Stingray City at least once — it’s genuinely different from a normal beach day. Standing in waist-deep water while rays glide past is the moment most families remember from this stop. Pair it with a shorter Seven Mile Beach visit rather than trying to fit both at full length. — Paid days Port Adventures filter check Run toddler, swim-comfort, and Disney-vs-independent filters before you book a boat day — the ship-wait guarantee matters more on tender ports. pages.description: Juneau Disney Cruise Line port guide: Mendenhall Glacier, whale watching, downtown walking, cool-weather packing, food, shopping, safety, and timing.
pages.body: Juneau Port Guide — Disney Cruise Day Ashore | Cruising Cove Cruising Cove Menu Ships Ports Onboard Dining Entertainment Plan My Cruise planner What it costs Deposit & final payment Booking windows Castaway Club Embarkation day Kids clubs Gratuities Wi-Fi packages Seasickness Accessibility June 2026 changes Stateroom guides Compare sailings Packing list Special sailings Excursions Pirate Night FAQ Articles Community Gallery Marketplace Find an Agent Port of call · Alaska Juneau. Alaska’s capital, reachable only by boat or plane — glacier views, whales, and a compact downtown are all within reach of the pier, if you dress for the weather. — Quick facts At a glance Region Alaska (capital city) Dock type Pier, downtown Currency USD Language English Best known for Mendenhall Glacier Common on Alaska / Inside Passage — The day Three clean options Juneau packs a lot into one call: glacier , wildlife on the water , or downtown on foot . Unlike most Caribbean ports, the pier drops you right into the small downtown core — the harder decision is how far out of town to go for the glacier or whale-watching boats. Signature sight Mendenhall Glacier A drive-up glacier with a visitor center, viewpoints, and (conditions permitting) trails to nearby falls — no hiking required to see it well. Wildlife Whale watching Humpback sightings are common on Juneau boat tours in season — one of the more reliable whale-watching stops on an Alaska itinerary. Low transfer Downtown on foot Compact, walkable streets right off the pier — shops, the Red Dog Saloon, and a tram to mountain views without a long transfer. — Transportation How far is everything? Destination From the pier How most families go Notes Downtown Juneau Right at the pier Walk One of the few Alaska stops where downtown is literally dockside Mount Roberts Tramway Adjacent to the pier Walk to the tram base, then ride up Fast way to mountain views without a hike or a long drive Mendenhall Glacier ~20–30 min Shuttle, taxi, or Port Adventure Popular independent shuttles run regularly from downtown Whale-watching departure points Boats often depart near downtown or a short shuttle away Booked tour Confirm your exact meeting point when you book No rental-car necessity. Downtown, the tram, and many tour meeting points are all walkable from the pier — a real difference from most Caribbean stops. Independent shuttles. Mendenhall Glacier shuttles are common and simpler than a formal excursion for families comfortable arranging their own return time. Disney transfer. Worth it for glacier or whale-watching days when you want the ship-wait guarantee on a boat- or drive-based tour. See Port Adventures filters . — Food What to eat ashore Fresh seafood. Wild Alaska salmon and halibut show up on nearly every downtown menu — a fish-and-chips stand or a sit-down spot both work for a short window. Tracy’s King Crab Shack–style stands. Dockside crab and chowder stands are a Juneau tradition for cruise passengers — expect a line at peak times. Downtown cafés. Coffee shops and bakeries are an easy warm-up stop if the weather turns cool or wet. Kids. Alaska’s rainiest big port — and one of its most rewarding, with Creek Street’s boardwalks, the world’s largest collection of totem poles, and fishing right off the dock. — Quick facts At a glance Region Alaska Dock type Pier, downtown Currency USD Language English Best known for Creek Street + totems Weather Rain, most days — The day Three clean options Ketchikan splits into Creek Street and downtown , a totem-pole and culture stop , or a fishing or floatplane excursion out over Misty Fjords. Bring rain gear no matter which you pick — this is Alaska’s rainforest port, and dry days are the exception, not the rule. Low transfer Creek Street & downtown Boardwalk buildings on stilts over the creek, small shops, and salmon-viewing platforms during the run — all a short walk from the pier. Culture stop Totem parks Home to the world’s largest collection of totem poles, split across a few sites (some downtown, some a short ride out) with Tlingit, Haida, and Tsimshian heritage. Signature excursion Fishing / Misty Fjords Salmon fishing charters are a Ketchikan classic; floatplane or boat tours into Misty Fjords National Monument run on clearer days. — Transportation How far is everything? Creek Street and much of downtown are steps from the pier, so a rainy day doesn’t have to mean a wasted call. Disney transfer. Worth it for fishing charters or floatplane tours where weather-driven schedule changes make the ship-wait guarantee valuable. See Port Adventures filters . — Food What to eat ashore Fresh salmon and halibut. Ketchikan calls itself the salmon capital of the world for good reason — grilled or fried, it’s the local specialty to look for. Creek Street cafés. Small waterfront spots along the boardwalk make a good rainy-day lunch stop with a view of the creek. Fishing-day catch. Some charters offer to have your catch processed and shipped — ask before you book if that matters to you. Kids. Simple chowder or fish-and-chips spots downtown beat waiting out weather for a fancier reservation. — Shopping What’s worth bringing home Alaska Native art and carvings. Look for authenticity markers if you want genuine Tlingit, Haida, or Tsimshian work — totem park gift shops are a good place to start. Rain gear (yes, really). If you underpacked, downtown outfitters sell exactly what you need for the rest of the sailing. Cruise-line jewelry chains. Present here as in most Alaska ports — fine to browse, not the local specialty. — Safety With kids in daylight Downtown Ketchikan and Creek Street are compact, well-trafficked, and generally very safe in daylight. Wet boardwalks and wooden stairs on Creek Street get slippery — good grip shoes matter more than style. Floatplane and fishing charters are weather-dependent; operators cancel or reroute for safety, so build flexibility into your day rather than fighting the schedule. Layered, waterproof clothing is a safety issue as much as a comfort one — cold, wet kids tire and complain fast. — Timing Work backward from all-aboard Day type Realistic clock Buffer tip Creek Street + downtown 2–3 hours Easy buffer; a rainy day doesn’t derail this plan Totem park visit Half day Confirm shuttle or taxi return timing before you leave downtown Fishing charter Half to full day Weather and fish activity can shift timing — ask the outfitter about typical delays Misty Fjords floatplane / boat tour Half day Most weather-sensitive excursion in this port — have a downtown backup plan — Don’t miss this Ketchikan’s biggest timing risk is weather-driven cancellations , not distance. Disney's second Bahamian destination, opened in 2024 — built around authentic Bahamian culture rather than classic Disney theming, with one of the best beaches in the fleet's ports. — Quick facts At a glance Opened June 2024 Location Eleuthera, Bahamas Size ~900 acres Distance from Castaway Cay ~120 miles Beaches 2 (family + Serenity Bay) Kids club Sebastian's Cove, ages 3-10 — The island What's different here Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point sits on a peninsula on the southern tip of Eleuthera — not a fully private island like Castaway Cay, but a privately controlled section of a larger, inhabited island. Disney purchased the property in 2019 and opened it to guests in June 2024. Where Castaway Cay leans into classic Disney character theming, Lookout Cay is built around Bahamian culture, art, and conservation, including a Goombay Cultural Center celebrating Junkanoo traditions. One real difference worth knowing before you go: Castaway Cay's beaches sit behind a breakwater, so the water is calm and sheltered. Lighthouse Point's beaches are unsheltered, so conditions can be more variable — often beautiful, but worth checking conditions if you're planning to swim with young kids. — What's there Beaches and activities Mabrika Cove — the main family beach, stretching the length of the common area Serenity Bay Beach — the adults-only section, with its own BBQ and the Blue Hole Bar Rush Out Gush Out — a water playground for kids Goombay Cultural Center — live Junkanoo performances and local art Sebastian's Cove — the island's kids' club, ages 3–10 A network of elevated bridges over the coastline, built to protect the natural dune habitat — Worth booking early Cabanas Twenty premium family cabanas are available near the family beach, including four double cabanas for larger groups with massage service add-ons. Six additional adult cabanas are available at Serenity Bay. As with Castaway Cay, these book up fast once the reservation window opens. Use the booking-window helper for your Castaway Club tier countdown. — Which island? Lookout Cay vs Castaway Cay Lookout Cay is Disney’s newest Bahamas day — bigger beaches and culture-forward design. Castaway Cay is still the easier classic for snorkelers and little kids. A short walk from the pier into downtown — and an easy place to overspend or overheat. Pick beach, town, or Atlantis before you step off. — Quick facts At a glance Region Bahamas Dock type Pier (usually) To downtown Walkable Currency BSD ≈ USD Common on 3–4 night Biggest trap Doing too much — The day Pick one job for the day Nassau works best when you pick one job for the day: town stroll, beach club, or Atlantis-area day. Mixing all three usually means heat, queues, and a rushed return. Many Wish-class and Dream-class Bahamas itineraries call here — check your Navigator app for dock side and all-aboard. Low spend · walkable Town day Straw Market, Bay Street, Parliament Square photos, a conch lunch, and back aboard with time to spare. Swim day Beach club / Junkanoo Chair, shade, and water. Junkanoo Beach is close; club packages add food and transfers. Big ticket Atlantis / Paradise Island Aquaventure + marine exhibits — plan tickets, transfer, and heat. Worth it when everyone wants the water park energy. — Transportation How far is everything? Destination From the pier How most families go Notes Downtown / Bay Street ~5–15 min walk Walk Stay on main tourist corridors with kids; agree a meeting spot Junkanoo Beach ~15–25 min walk or short taxi Walk or taxi Public beach — bring cash for chairs/umbrellas if offered Atlantis / Paradise Island ~15–30 min by taxi / shuttle Disney Port Adventure, taxi, or Atlantis transfer Bridge toll / return traffic can stretch the ride Farther beach clubs 20–45+ min Booked transfer (Disney or club) Transfer time eats swim time — read the schedule Taxis. Horse carts and hop-on buses exist near the pier — fun photos for some, pressure sales for others. You’re allowed to say no and keep walking. Disney transfer. Worth it when your day is Atlantis or a distant club and you want the ship-wait cushion. See Nassau Port Adventure filters . — Disney vs independent What to book, what to skip Nassau is usually a docked call (not a tender), which makes independent exploring easier than Grand Cayman–style tender ports — but the clock and heat still punish over-ambition. Book Disney when: you’re doing Atlantis / a farther beach club, traveling with little kids, or you want the ship-wait cushion if a transfer runs late. Go independent when: you’re staying near the pier (town stroll, Junkanoo Beach), you’re comfortable with taxis, and you’ll reverse-plan from all-aboard with a real buffer. Skip: stacking Atlantis + Straw Market + a “quick” second beach. Pick one job for the day. Skip: following every pier greeter into a shop or tour you didn’t research — smile, decline, keep walking. Worth the Disney excursion filter: see Nassau Port Adventures if you want curated options with return protection. — Tender note If your itinerary ever lists a tender or unusual dock assignment, trust Navigator over habit — Nassau is typically pier-side for DCL, but weather and port operations can change the day. — Food What to eat ashore Worth leaving for. Fresh conch (salad, fritters, cracked conch) and a cold drink in the town or beach zone — not a multi-course commitment. Tourist markup. Pier-adjacent menus exist to catch you in the first 200 yards. Walk a few blocks if you want slightly better value. Short window. If you’re on a tight all-aboard, eat aboard or keep it to a known beach-club lunch included in a package. Kids. Beach clubs with familiar grill menus beat hunting for a perfect restaurant with a toddler who is already hot. — Shopping What’s worth bringing home Straw Market & Bay Street. Souvenirs, bags, shirts — expect bargaining. Decide a max spend before you walk in. Duty-free / jewelry. Fine if that’s your thing; compare to prices you’d pay at home, including the “cruise discount” pitch. Skip pressure. Pier greeters steering you into specific shops are doing a job. You can smile, decline, and follow your own map. — Safety With kids in daylight Stay in well-trafficked tourist areas: Bay Street corridor, Beach / Paradise Island with a plan, known clubs. Don’t wander into residential side streets “just to see” with strollers and no map — daylight downtown tourist zones are the easy mode. Watch bags in crowds near the pier and markets. Same city-cruise common sense as any busy port. Sun is the real hazard: hats, water, shade breaks. Nassau heat plus walking can end a day faster than any scam. — Timing Work backward from all-aboard Day type Realistic clock Buffer tip Town stroll 2–4 hours Easy to pad; leave downtown 60+ minutes before all-aboard if you dawdle Junkanoo Beach Half day Walk time both ways + rinse/change Beach club package Most of the call Obey the club’s return shuttle, not your optimism Atlantis water park Nearly full day Tickets + transfer + lunch add up — start early, leave early — Don’t miss this If you only have energy for one “Nassau moment,” many families pick a real swim (Junkanoo or a club) over another hour of shops. The pier shopping will still be there on the walk back. — Don’t miss The one thing locals and repeats push Get in the water or get a real local bite — don’t only do the pier retail strip. Bay Street is convenient; it is not the whole island. A Gold Rush-era town small enough to walk end to end, with the White Pass & Yukon Route train as the classic reason to book ahead. — Quick facts At a glance Region Alaska Dock type Pier, downtown Currency USD Language English Best known for White Pass & Yukon train Common on Alaska / Inside Passage — The day Three clean options Skagway is one of the most compact, walkable ports on an Alaska itinerary. Most calls come down to the train , a wider Klondike-area tour , or a slow downtown walk through preserved Gold Rush storefronts. The historic district sits steps from the pier. Signature excursion White Pass & Yukon Route A narrow-gauge railway climbing steep grades toward the Yukon border, with scenery that draws people back to Skagway specifically for the ride. Book ahead — it sells out. Bigger loop Klondike Highway / Yukon day Van or coach tours push farther into the mountains than the train alone, often combining scenery with a stop at a summit or lake. Low transfer Downtown Gold Rush walk Wooden boardwalks, preserved 1898-era buildings, and small museums — all within a few blocks of where the ship docks. — Transportation How far is everything? Destination From the pier How most families go Notes Historic downtown Short walk Walk The whole historic district is walkable in well under an hour White Pass & Yukon Route depot Short walk from most piers Walk to the depot, then train Book your seat ahead of the sailing — popular departures sell out Klondike Highway / Yukon tours Departs near downtown Booked coach or van tour Longer commitment than the train alone; confirm return timing Dyea / Chilkoot Trail area ~15–20 min drive Taxi or tour Quieter, less-visited history stop for a slower-paced call Walk-everything port. Unlike most cruise stops, you may not need a taxi at all if downtown and the train depot are your day. Book the train early. The White Pass & Yukon Route is Skagway’s single most in-demand activity — popular departure times fill up well before the sailing. Disney transfer. Worth considering for Klondike Highway or Yukon-area tours that go farther from town. See Port Adventures filters . — Food What to eat ashore Downtown cafés and bakeries. Small, walkable options serve chowder, sandwiches, and reindeer sausage — easy for a short window. Historic saloons. A few of the preserved Gold Rush-era buildings house restaurants and bars leaning into the theme — fun for a photo stop and a meal. Train day. Some White Pass departures are timed tightly with the ship — grab food before or after, not mid-tour. Kids. Simple sandwich and soup spots downtown beat trying to squeeze in a sit-down meal on a train-day schedule. — Shopping What’s worth bringing home Gold Rush and local history items. Skagway leans hard into its 1898 heritage — books, prints, and small museum-shop items make a more distinctive souvenir than generic cruise trinkets. Alaska-made goods. Local art, jewelry, and food items are sold alongside the same cruise-line jewelry chains found in other ports. Small footprint. Downtown is compact enough that browsing the whole main street takes well under an hour — easy to combine with the train or a walk. — Safety With kids in daylight Downtown Skagway is small, walkable, and generally very low-crime in daylight. Wooden boardwalks and uneven historic-district surfaces can be slippery when wet — good shoes matter more than fashion here. Train routes run along steep grades and cliffside views — keep kids seated and away from open vestibule areas per crew instructions. Weather shifts quickly in the mountains; dress in layers even if the morning looks mild at the pier. — Timing Work backward from all-aboard Day type Realistic clock Buffer tip Downtown walk only 1–3 hours Very easy buffer — one of the lowest-risk ports for timing White Pass & Yukon train Half day (varies by route chosen) Excursion trains are typically scheduled around the ship’s call — still confirm your specific departure Klondike Highway / Yukon tour Most of the call Longer commitment; prefer booked tours with a stated return guarantee Train + downtown combo Half to most of the call Easy to pair since downtown sits right at the train depot — Don’t miss this Skagway is forgiving on timing compared to most Alaska stops — the harder problem is booking the train early enough , not fitting it into your day. Certain dates on certain ships get a full extra layer of theming. Here's what's running in 2026, and which ship and itinerary each one lives on. — Booking How themed sailings work Halloween, Very Merrytime, Marvel Day at Sea, and Pixar Day at Sea are overlays on select sailings — not separate tickets. You book a normal cruise on an eligible date; the theming is included. High-demand holiday weeks sell out early, and Castaway Club booking windows still control when you can reserve cabanas, dining, and Port Adventures. Activity windows: same Castaway Club calendar as any other sailing — booking window helper . Final payment: still due on Disney’s timeline before most online activity booking — deposit & final payment . Packing: costumes are optional but common on Halloween / Very Merrytime — see the Halloween packing section and Pirate Night guide. — Superheroes at sea Marvel Day at Sea Marvel Day at Sea returns on the Disney Magic for 4- and 5-night Western Caribbean itineraries out of Galveston, Texas starting January 2026 — the first time this event sails from Galveston (Magic has hosted Marvel Day on other itineraries since 2017). Over 30 heroes and villains appear across the day, including Spider-Man, Captain America, Captain Marvel, Thor, Loki, and Black Panther — plus a USO-style tribute show honoring Captain America in Fathoms and warrior training with Okoye in the atrium. The day builds to a deck party themed around a clash between heroes and villains. Book early if Marvel is the reason you’re sailing — these dates are easy to miss once verandah inventory thins out. Confirm your specific voyage is labeled Marvel Day at Sea in Disney’s booking tools before you deposit. — Pixar pals Pixar Day at Sea Pixar Day at Sea returns on the Disney Fantasy , sailing 5-night Bahamian itineraries from Port Canaveral, Florida, stopping at Nassau, Castaway Cay, and Lookout Cay at Lighthouse Point. Expect appearances from beloved Pixar characters throughout the day, capped off with a Pixar Pals Celebration deck party in the evening. — Seasonal favorites Halloween on the High Seas & Very Merrytime Cruises Halloween on the High Seas runs on select September–October sailings across the fleet — Pumpkin Tree lighting, Mickey’s Mouse-querade, trick-or-treating, seasonal menus, and Halloween character costumes. Destiny joins the celebration for 2026; full rundown: Halloween on the Destiny . Very Merrytime Cruises bring holiday theming to U.S.-based DCL ships in the winter season — tree lightings, holiday characters, and festive entertainment layered onto regular itineraries. Treat these like peak holiday demand: book earlier than a random January sailing, and expect higher fares around Christmas and New Year’s weeks. — Character-themed sailings Bluey & other family favorites 2026 also brings Bluey and Bingo–themed experiences to select sailings on the Disney Dream , Disney Wish , and returning Disney Wonder (San Diego, fall 2026), aimed at families with younger kids. Details: Bluey on Disney Cruise Line in 2026 . — Worth knowing What isn't currently running — Status check Star Wars Day at Sea has run on Disney Cruise Line in the past and is frequently requested by fans, but is not part of the confirmed 2026 lineup as of this writing. Worth verifying current availability before booking a sailing specifically for it.
